correctness_confidence.basis: All explicit integer inequalities (7^100 < 2^281, Schönhage m=3,4 tau-bounds), Z[eps] polynomial cancellations, Strassen operation counts, Freivalds bounds (k(6n^2-2n), 2^-30, 16^-10), dyadic ratios n^(9/4)/n^2 = 2^k, and Vandermonde alternating-binomial kernel proofs are mathematically valid and verified.

rigor.basis: The zero-float exact-Z/Q certification approach avoids numerical epsilon-cancellation pitfalls, and Section 4 explicitly separates mechanized claims from imported literature theorems. Minor gaps include omitted index bounds in Theorems 2.1(2) and 3.1 and unproved exact-rank lower bounds (R=3, 13, 25) in the text.

novelty.basis: The mathematical components—Strassen (1969), Schönhage (1981), Freivalds (1979), Vandermonde nullspaces, and Chen's decision-tree reduction (2026)—are known; the contribution lies in packaging them into a unified float-free Lean 4.36.0 and exact-Z/Q certificate suite rather than proving new theorems.

significance.basis: Provides a clean, auditable verification baseline that prevents floating-point artifacts in border-rank tau-theorem bounds and clearly separates unconditional omega_ver = omega_C from the conditional omega_C = 9/4 assumption, though impact is bounded because the deep reductions remain external.

reproducibility.basis: All numerical witnesses, integer power inequalities, polynomial identities, and Vandermonde kernel vectors are explicitly stated in the PDF and independently hand-checkable without external artifacts, backed by stated Lean 4.36.0 theorem mappings (T01-T20) and SHA-256 certificate IDs (C01-C16).

summary: This manuscript presents MATVER-BORDERRANK-CERT-1.0, a float-free exact-Z/Q and Lean 4.36.0 certification suite inspired by Xiangle Chen's proof (arXiv:2611.34814v1) equating deterministic matrix-product verification with omega_C. Section 4 transparently discloses that Chen's decision-tree reduction and Schönhage's tau-theorem are imported rather than re-proved in Lean; the paper certifies the exact algebraic machinery across 20 Lean theorems and 16 certificates (C01-C16). All explicit calculations in the PDF are sound: Strassen's 64-entry identity and 7^100 < 2^281 (omega < 2.81); Z[eps] border-rank witnesses for T_dual (R_under <= 2) and Schönhage's family T_{m,n} (R_under <= mn+1) with pure-integer proofs of omega < 2.70 and omega < 2.55; decision-tree ceiling algebra and exact n^(9/4)/n^2 = 2^k separation ratios; Freivalds costs k(6n^2-2n) and error bounds (2^-30 < 10^-9, 16^-10 < 10^-12); and constructive rational Vandermonde nullspace witnesses blocking low-rank linear probes. Minor notational omissions aside, no mathematical errors were found.
strengths: Exact float-free integer power certificates (7^100 < 2^281; m=3 and m=4 Schönhage tau-bounds) eliminate floating-point logarithm approximations rigorously.
All explicit Z[eps] polynomial cancellations in Theorem 2.1, Freivalds operation counts k(6n^2 - 2n), and Vandermonde kernel witnesses in Theorem 3.1 are algebraically exact.
Section 4 maintains a clear, honest verification boundary separating Lean-checked algebraic identities from imported literature theorems ([3], [6]) and the unrefereed omega_C = 9/4 assumption.
weaknesses: The deep complexity-theoretic results (Chen's decision-tree border-rank reduction and Schönhage's asymptotic sum inequality) are imported externally rather than formalized in Lean.
Theorem 2.1(1) omits writing out the output-vector combination M_1 e_2 + M_2(eps e_1 - e_2) = eps T_dual + O(eps^2) and does not prove the lower bounds R_under >= 2 or R = 3.
Theorem 2.1(2) omits explicit index ranges for R_i and C_j (0 <= i < m-1, 0 <= j < n-1) and omits proofs for the exact-rank lower bounds R >= 13 and R >= 25.
Theorem 3.1 omits explicit 0-based index bounds (0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n-1, n >= 2) for R_{i,j} = (i+1)^j, and Section 3.1 omits the trivial upper bound omega_ver <= omega_C in the sandwich.
The paper's title sounds broader than its actual contribution, which is formalizing elementary algebraic witnesses and corollaries rather than proving verification-vs-computation equivalence.
strong_novelty_candidates: Integer-power zero-float certification of Schönhage tau-theorem exponent ceilings (omega < 2.70 and omega < 2.55) paired with exact Z[eps] direct-sum witnesses in Lean 4.36.0.
Constructive rational Vandermonde alternating-binomial nullspace witnesses explicitly demonstrating the oblivious low-rank linear-probe derandomization barrier.
